alignments.note: 'up' is part of the ASV's fixed rendering of חָנַךְ and adds no direction or result of its own; head stays on the verb (rule 44). Competing reading marks 'up' added.
The ASV writes the object bare, leaving the לְ nothing to say (rule 40).
Assimilated article: the ASV writes 'a child' and no 'the' (rules 12, 29).
Supplied indefinite article joins the noun (rule 15).
עַל־פִּי, a preposition with its construct noun, rendered by the single word 'in'; headed on the construct noun (rule 30).

The ASV recasts the one nominal דַּרְכּוֹ as 'the way he should go'; the supplied verb is what the noun's own lexeme names and joins its unit (rule 46's closing paragraph). Head kept on 'way', which writes the lexeme directly; 'go' was the competing head.
Suffix realized by the subject pronoun of the recast relative clause (rule 18).
Supplied coordinator: no conjunction morpheme stands at the head of this clause (rule 14's closing sentences); גַּם takes the 'even' beside it.
כִּי rendered by the temporal subordinator the ASV wrote for it (rule 55).
Hiphil 'be old' rendered by copula and adjective; headed on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 44).
Subject pronoun and auxiliary stay with the finite verb (rule 17); unit discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).

review_notes: The Hebrew gloss 'according to his way' was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
